objections.objection: The revise_plan case is grounded entirely on plan_line observations of what L1-L3 say (ev_initial_entry_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa_1..3, ev_initial_entry_bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb_1..3). None of these ids establishes the absence of an external spec, appendix, or runbook, yet the load-bearing completeness assumption (plan-is-complete / no-hidden-detail) is marked unverified in the critique. The underspecification findings therefore rest on an unproven negative.
objections.wouldChangeRecommendation: If a linked spec supplying the validation contract, flag config, and rollback thresholds exists, the underspecification evidence collapses and accept_plan becomes viable; confirming plan.md has no linked appendix (the assumptions' own how_to_verify) would keep revise_plan.

objections.objection: The missing-observability finding infers absence of monitoring capability from mere absence of a monitoring step in the plan text. A delta-only three-line plan can legitimately rely on pre-existing error-rate telemetry, so ev_initial_entry_bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb_4 does not ground a real gap and should not on its own force revision.
objections.wouldChangeRecommendation: Verifying that no error-rate telemetry pre-exists in the system would restore this risk's weight; confirming existing telemetry would drop it from the revise_plan rationale without changing the position.

objections.objection: Treating plan.md:L1-L3 as the complete and only artifact frames underspecification as a defect of the plan rather than of the review scope. The same evidence is equally consistent with a deliberately terse delta plan that references controls defined elsewhere; the framing pre-selects revise_plan over needs_more_evidence.
objections.wouldChangeRecommendation: If the frozen context cannot resolve whether an external appendix exists, needs_more_evidence is the more defensible position; establishing the artifact boundary would restore revise_plan.

objections.objection: The recommendation leans on the L3 rollback gate being unenforceable (no baseline, threshold, window, mechanism per ev_initial_entry_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa_3 / ev_initial_entry_bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb_3), but this same defect, if the safety gate can never fire, is severe enough to argue reject_plan rather than a light revise. The logic does not justify why revision suffices instead of rejection for a non-functional safety control.
objections.wouldChangeRecommendation: If the rollback criterion cannot be made enforceable by a bounded edit (i.e., no baseline data exists to define a threshold), reject_plan is warranted; if quantifying it is a trivial non-destructive edit, revise_plan holds.
